project: Personal video tool for the English AI-avatar YouTube channel 'Sit With Pastor Sam'
language_of_videos: English (en-US). Everything the viewer sees or hears is in English.
language_of_user: French. Talk to the user in French.
goal: A personal tool that turns one video idea from the lists below into a finished long-form YouTube video for this AI-avatar channel: the script, the voice, lip-synced avatar clips, B-roll (AI-generated and free stock), verse/text cards, subtitles, the final edit and the publishing pack.

video_method.source: Jake Trinder, 'How to Become Disgustingly Good at YouTube' (youtu.be/Dx-c19qXdxM), Oct 14 2026
video_method.principle: A video is a series system: topic, packaging (title + thumbnail), hook, body and edit must all be right; one wrong decision can sink the video.
topic: Pick topics from what the audience already chooses to watch (revealed preference), not from what we think they need.
For each topic note the floor (median views of a decent video) and the ceiling (best videos) over the last 3–6 months, 8+ min videos.
Check views look real (≈1–5 % likes per view, on-topic comments) and that demand is still active (recent videos still getting views).
Raise the ceiling by attaching the topic to a bigger demand: season, event, culture (Amish, Japanese), well-known store (Walmart, Costco, Aldi).
title: Use a title framing that wins in at least 2–3 different channels or niches, not a single outlier.
Understand why the framing works and only reuse it if that reason is true for our audience (avoid overfitting).
The title must make a promise the video fully delivers; never use false words.
thumbnail: Job 1: stand out in the feed. Job 2: be understood at a glance.
Avatar face + one object/icon that targets the audience + a tension that opens a question; the title closes only part of it.
video_method.edit: The edit matches the promise: calm and warm for our characters, useful B-roll, on-screen text for numbers, no gratuitous effects.

hook_4P.promise: Confirm in one sentence that this is what they clicked for.
hook_4P.proof: Why listen: honest proof only (sources, the character's story told as a story, a shown result). Never fake credentials or numbers.
hook_4P.plan: Announce the steps / number of items and what comes at the end.
hook_4P.persona: Name the viewer: 'if you're over 60', 'if you lost your spouse', 'wenn du einen Diesel fährst'.
hook_4P.timing: All 4 P inside the first 30–45 seconds.

body_acceptance_criteria: Decompose the title's promise: what must be true at the end for the title to be true? Break each answer down again.
That list is the outline; the script is finished only when every condition is met.
Deliver real value fast, then exceed the expectation (one bonus item, a safety tip, a worked example).
Goal is viewer satisfaction, not retention tricks.
after_publish: Early signals: positive comments per view (and what they say), likes per view, subs per view, view curve vs channel average.
A metric tells where to look, not what to change (low CTR → look at the thumbnail and ask why).
Sharp retention drop → inspect that moment (early CTA, a slow part) and cut it.
Write down one lesson per video for the next one.
pre_production_checklist: Topic has a good floor (median) and a high ceiling on videos from the last 3–6 months.
Reference views look real and demand is still active.
Topic is attached to a bigger demand when possible (season, store, culture, event).
Title framing wins in at least 2 different channels and we know why it works for our audience.
Title promise is deliverable and true, no false words.
Thumbnail: avatar face, one audience-targeting object, an open question; understood in 1 second.
Hook has the 4 P (promise, honest proof, plan, persona) in the first 45 seconds.
Script outline = the list of conditions that make the title true; every one is met.
Over-deliver: a bonus, a safety tip, a worked example.
Edit matches the promise: calm, warm, no gratuitous effects.
After 48 h and 7 days: read comments, likes/view, subs/view, retention curve; note one lesson.

title_rule: Clone, word for word, the title of a video that got many views and change only the niche words. If a word would be false for our video ('BANNED', '100% Effective', 'NEVER EXPIRE', an inflated number, 'Industry Buried'), replace only that word. The new ideas below already follow this rule and the video_method.
avatar_rules: Each lip-synced avatar clip is at most 15 seconds; longer passages are split and alternated with B-roll.
Every avatar image comes from the same reference image (same face, clothes, set) — generate the reference first, then use it for every variant.
Faces must stay clearly visible (three-quarter angle at most) or lip-sync fails.
Cover any glitchy lip-sync moment with B-roll while the voice continues.
The avatar is on screen 25–35 % of the time in teachings and sermons, and only 10–15 % in prayer videos.

free_stock_sources.name: Pexels
free_stock_sources.license: Pexels License: free for commercial use, no attribution required; do not imply endorsement.

stock_rules: Search in English, landscape 1080p or 4K, 25/30 fps.
Log every clip in credits.csv (file, source, URL, license, date).
Re-check each license page before first use.

editing.subtitles: Upload an English SRT made from the script.
editing.music: Soft, royalty-free, −25 to −30 dB under the voice; no copyrighted hymns or songs recorded by others.
editing.transitions: Slow cross-fades, gentle zooms, no flashy effects (the promise is calm and warm).

script_output_schema.title: string

reference_videos.title: string

script_output_schema.estimated_minutes: number (≈130 spoken words per minute for these slow voices)
acceptance_criteria: the conditions that make the title true (from video_method) — each must be met

segments.part: Hook | Welcome | Item 1 … | Prayer | Blessing | Ending
segments.speaker: PASTOR
segments.shot: one of the channel shot_library keys, or BROLL_STOCK / BROLL_AI / TEXT_CARD / VERSE_CARD
segments.voice_text: English text spoken during this segment (the voice continues under B-roll)
segments.est_seconds: number — max 15 for any lip-synced avatar shot
segments.on_screen_text: short overlay, verse reference, number, or empty

production_pipeline: 1. Pick the next video (publishing_order, then new_ideas_oct2026 by priority) or the one the user names.
2. Research: open the reference video(s), read the transcript, note structure and promise; check floor/ceiling and that demand is still active (video_method.topic).
3. Write acceptance criteria from the title (video_method.body_acceptance_criteria), then the script with the 4P hook in the first 45 s.
4. Fact-check every claim: exact KJV text for every verse; teachings, sermons and prayers follow the channel formats. Remove anything unsourced.
5. Check the word count against the channel target.
6. Voice: generate audio per segment with the fixed voice of the speaker.
7. Avatar clips: lip-sync each avatar segment on the right reference image (≤15 s).
8. B-roll: stock first for generic real scenes, AI for specific scenes and for anything showing our characters' places.
9. Edit: voice track, avatar clips, B-roll, text/verse cards, music, subtitles, AI label in the first seconds.
10. QA with video_method.pre_production_checklist and the channel guardrails, export.
11. Publishing pack: title, description (template), chapters, tags, pinned comment, thumbnail; tick 'Altered or synthetic content' in YouTube Studio.
12. After 48 h and 7 days: read the signals listed in video_method.after_publish and write one lesson for the next video.
compliance: AI characters are declared in the channel description and with YouTube's 'altered or synthetic content' setting on every upload.
The characters' memories are presented as stories; they never claim to be real people or give fake credentials.
Affiliate links and the channels' own products are clearly labelled (FTC).
No medical, legal or financial promises.

existing_scripts.note: Finished scripts in the repo — use them as style examples (plain text, pasted into the Subscriber app).

channel.about:
Beloved, come sit with me a while.

This channel is a quiet place to open the Bible together and talk about the questions that matter most in the later years of life. What happens when we die? Will we see our loved ones again? Why am I still here? How do I keep holding on when God seems silent?
Every week you’ll find Bible teaching that answers one real question with Scripture, short sermons for hard seasons, and an evening prayer to end your day in peace.
New teachings every Tuesday and Thursday. Evening prayer every Sunday.
📖 Heaven and Hope — A Bible Study for Your Later Years: [your link]
🎁 Free download — 10 Bible Promises About Heaven: [your link]
Pastor Samuel is an AI-presented Bible teacher. Scripture quotations are from the King James Version (public domain). This channel never asks for donations or offerings. If you are going through a hard time, please also reach out to a local church or someone you trust.

character.name: Pastor Samuel Brooks ("Pastor Sam")
character.bio: Grew up in a small country town in rural Georgia, son of a farmer and a church pianist. Led a small country church for forty years. Married 41 years to Mae, who went home to the Lord three years ago. Two children, five grandchildren. Still reads the old King James Bible his mother gave him. Morning coffee on the porch; evening study in his small home study.
character.why: His story lets him speak about grief, old age and God's faithfulness gently and from the inside.
character.tone: Slow, warm, never threatening. Teaches like a grandfather, not like a shouting preacher.

fixed_lines.opening: Beloved, come sit with me a while.
fixed_lines.comfort: You are not forgotten. Not by Him.
fixed_lines.blessing: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee… (Numbers 6:24–26)

never: Ask for money, donations, 'seed offerings' or 'buy me a coffee'.
Promise healing or a blessing in exchange for watching, sharing or doing something.
Present himself as a real living pastor or name a real church; memories are told as stories ('Let me tell you a story…').
Reuse words or audio of real preachers.
Use 'GOD SAYS: I BEG YOU' style manipulative messages.

voice: African American man around 68, deep, warm, slightly husky, slow pace with natural pauses (2–3 s between prayer sentences), gentle Southern accent. Same voice ID for every video.
bible: Quote only the King James Version word for word (public domain). NIV/ESV/NLT are copyrighted: short quotes only with the source. Stay on doctrine widely shared by Christians; Enoch or extra-biblical books only in small doses, saying clearly what is and isn't in the Bible.

structure: The question head-on (avatar close-up), with the 4P hook.
Welcome: 'Beloved, come sit with me a while.' Why the question matters; which series it belongs to.
What people believe, gently corrected. B-roll: old family photos, old hands, peaceful cemetery.
4–5 answers from the Bible: verse card (KJV), simple explanation, a life example; avatar at the start and end of each answer, B-roll in the middle.
What it changes for you today — the most personal moment.
A 2–3 min prayer tied to the topic, calm B-roll.
Next episode of the series and the free guide. No money request.
The trial named ('Maybe you've been praying for something for years…').
The passage read slowly (e.g. Psalm 13, Isaiah 40:31).
A Bible story or an illustration (presented as such).
The call ('Tonight, I want you to…') and the prayer.

timeline: Welcome — porch at sunset, lantern lit, 2–3 avatar clips of 10–15 s. Soft voice, distant crickets, very low piano.
Beloved, come sit with me a while. The day is done now…
Evening verse card on dark background. Voice alone, then rain begins.
For the worries of the day — old hands joined, steaming tea, rainy window.
Lord, I bring you the worries I carried today…
For the family — old photo frames, house lit at night, front door.
Watch over my children, and my children's children…
For the tired body — bed with a throw, bedside lamp, glass of water, glasses.
You know every ache in this body. Give it rest tonight…
For the protection of the home — house at night from outside, light behind curtains, stars.
Be a wall of fire around this home tonight… (Zechariah 2:5)
Gratitude — sunset on mountains, birds flying home, candle; piano rises slightly.
Thank you for another day, Lord…
Psalms reading — open Bible by candlelight, pages turning, verses on screen; slower voice, rain.
Blessing — one avatar clip looking at the camera.
The LORD bless thee, and keep thee… Goodnight, beloved.
Rest — screen slowly darkens to a near-black starry sky; rain only; no text.

formats.teaching_end_prayer: 2–3 min tied to the topic: one avatar clip to introduce it, 4–6 B-roll shots, one verse card, one avatar clip for the blessing.

script_length.target_words: 4,600–4,950 words (always under 5,000) for teachings and sermons ≈ 30–35 min; prayers ≈ 2,500–3,500 words for 30 min with long pauses.
script_length.style: Plain text script, no stage directions inside the spoken text; verse references written out ('Psalm ninety-one, verse one').

PASTOR_STUDY_TALKS.use: Teachings and sermons: hook, welcome, start/end of each answer, personal moment.
PASTOR_STUDY_TALKS.prompt: A 68-year-old African American pastor with short salt-and-pepper hair and a neatly trimmed gray beard, sitting at an old wooden desk in a small, warm home study in a Southern country house, evening. He wears a black clergy shirt with a white tab clerical collar under a soft charcoal wool cardigan. An open, well-worn leather King James Bible lies on the desk in front of him, one hand resting on the page. He looks gently straight into the camera, speaking softly with a warm, compassionate expression, mouth slightly open mid-sentence, face fully visible. Behind him, slightly out of focus: shelves of old books, a framed photo of an older woman, a brass desk lamp casting warm light, a window with dusk outside. Eye level, medium close-up, 50mm lens, f/2.8, shallow depth of field, realistic skin texture with natural wrinkles, documentary photography style, peaceful atmosphere, 16:9.
PASTOR_STUDY_TALKS.note: New reference image for the study set (the page only had porch prompts). Generate it from the porch 'reading' image as reference so the face and clothes match.

PASTOR_EVENING_READING.prompt: A 68-year-old African American pastor with short salt-and-pepper hair and a neatly trimmed gray beard, sitting in a white wooden rocking chair on the front porch of a modest old Southern country house, early evening. He wears a black clergy shirt with a white tab clerical collar under a soft charcoal wool cardigan. He holds an open, well-worn leather Bible with both hands at chest height and is reading aloud from it, mouth slightly open mid-sentence, eyes looking down at the page, head only slightly tilted so his face remains clearly visible in a three-quarter angle. A lit oil lantern glows on a small wooden side table beside him. Behind him, slightly out of focus: wooden porch railing, a quiet field and tall trees under a warm orange sunset sky fading to deep blue. Warm low light from the lantern and the sunset on his face. Eye level, medium shot, 50mm lens, f/2.8, shallow depth of field, realistic skin texture with natural wrinkles, documentary photography style, peaceful atmosphere, 16:9.

He holds the open Bible resting on his lap with one hand on the page, and has lifted his eyes from the Bible to look gently straight into the camera, speaking softly with a warm, compassionate expression, mouth slightly open mid-sentence. Face fully visible, relaxed shoulders. Eye level, medium shot, 50mm lens, f/2.8, shallow depth of field, realistic skin texture, documentary photography style, 16:9.

MOTION_TURN_PAGE.prompt: The pastor slowly turns a page of the Bible, then continues reading silently, subtle natural breathing, the lantern flame flickers gently, leaves move slightly in the evening breeze, very slow camera push-in.

MOTION_CLOSE_EYES_PRAY.use: Between two parts of a prayer.
MOTION_CLOSE_EYES_PRAY.prompt: The pastor gently closes the Bible on his lap, rests both hands on it, closes his eyes and bows his head slightly in quiet prayer, calm breathing, soft lantern flicker, static camera.

shot_library.negative_prompt: face hidden, head bowed too low, looking away from the book, cartoon, plastic skin, oversaturated, church interior, crowd, extra hands, extra fingers

VERSE_CARD.spec: Dark background, large serif text in light color, appears slowly; reference under it ('Psalm 91:1, KJV').

shot_library.reference_order: Generate the evening 'reading' image first and use it as the reference for every other Pastor image.

image_rules: Slow shots of 6–12 s, very light zoom, cross-fades, never hard cuts.
Warm low light: sunset, candle, lamp; nothing bright or saturated.
Objects rather than faces in B-roll: hands, cup, Bible, window, landscape.
Always the same 'house': same porch, candle, Bible — the channel becomes a familiar place.

broll.ai_broll: AI images of the porch, the Bible on the desk, the house at night, then 5–10 s image-to-video clips — keeps the same set as the avatar.
broll.bank: Prepare once 40–60 shots sorted by theme (family, night, protection, gratitude, Bible) and reuse them in every prayer.

subscriber_form.Other details: Warm low light, candles and lanterns, open King James Bible, no crowds, no megachurch stage, no readable logos, slow peaceful mood

sound: Voice first, with 2–3 s pauses between prayer sentences.
Soft constant rain under prayers, no loud thunder.
Royalty-free piano very low under the voice.
No hymns recorded by others (copyright claims).
